screens.heading: Self-Awareness
screens.body: Self-awareness is understanding yourself, your thoughts, feelings, and actions. It's like looking in a mirror and seeing yourself clearly, knowing what you need to work on, and how you affect others. It's a bit like being your own detective, noticing and understanding what makes you, you.

skills.name: Self-Compassion
skills.desc: Talk to yourself with the same kindness you would with a best friend.

skills.name: Emotional Awareness
skills.desc: Pay attenetion to your thoughts and feelings to understand yourself better. Name your feelings to tame your feelings.

skills.name: Honesty
skills.desc: Telling the trust to yourself about how you feel and what you do.

skills.name: Seeking Feedback
skills.desc: Ask for and listen to feedback from others to help you grow.

skills.name: Mindfulness
skills.desc: Stay present and aware of your emotions.

skills.name: Self-Reflection
skills.desc: Refelct on your experiences and learn from them to grow.

screens.heading: Activity: Compassion Web
screens.activity:
Holding a strand of wool, shout out something you like about yourself — then throw the wool pile to someone else. But don't let go of your strand!

Watch the web grow as everyone shares.
screens.note: Facilitator note: This visually shows connection and builds a warm, supportive atmosphere in the room.

screens.heading: What We Learned: Self-Awareness
screens.body: Self-compassion isn't about being "soft" or making excuses. It's about treating yourself the way you'd treat a friend. Building self-compassion helps with resilience, emotional awareness, and bouncing back from mistakes.

screens.heading: Activity: Glow & Grow
screens.activity:
Let's draw a picture in just 15 seconds!

If asked, give feedback using the "Glow & Grow" method:

• GLOW → Something they did well
• GROW → One way they could improve
screens.note: Facilitator note: This quick activity makes feedback feel safe and structured. Emphasise that both parts are equally important.

screens.heading: What We Learned: Seeking Feedback
screens.body: Giving and receiving feedback helps us grow by recognising our strengths ("Glows") and areas to improve ("Grows"). Practising this builds self-awareness, confidence, and a mindset that sees feedback as a tool for learning — not criticism.

screens.heading: What We Learned: Emotional Awareness
screens.body:
Emotional awareness helps us understand what's really going on beneath the surface. The better we understand our emotions, the better we understand ourselves and communicate with others.

Take the time to name your inner feelings, to help tame them.

screens.heading: Activity: Line of Honesty
screens.activity:
Answer each question by positioning yourself in the room.

One side of the line is 'Always' — the other is 'Never'

screens.heading: Honesty Scenarios
screens.instruction: Position yourself on the line — 'Always' on one side, 'Never' on the other.
scenarios: A friend tells you a secret, but someone else asks you about it. Do you keep it private?
Your best friend tells a joke that isn't funny, but they look excited for your reaction. Do you laugh anyway?
A teacher gives you credit for something you didn't do. Do you correct them or enjoy the moment?
Your teacher asks if you like their new shoes, but you don't. Do you tell the truth?
You accidentally break something at your homestay, but no one saw. Do you admit it?
You're talking to someone and they have something stuck in their teeth. Do you tell them?
You're part of a group chat where people are being mean. Do you leave it, or report it?

screens.heading: What We Learned: Honesty
screens.body: Practising honesty helps build self-awareness by allowing us to recognise our true feelings, take responsibility for our actions, and understand how our choices align with our values.

screens.heading: Activity: Ten Mindfulness Mini's
screens.activity: Follow along to try ten simple, quick ways to calm your mind, stay present, and reset your focus — anywhere, anytime!

items.label: Posture
items.desc: Sit up tall and feel grounded in your seat.

items.label: Deep Breathing
items.desc: Breathe in slowly through your nose, then out slowly through your mouth.

items.label: Balance
items.desc: Stand on one foot and find your centre.

items.label: Affirmation
items.desc: "I am calm and at peace." Say it — mean it.

items.label: Smile
items.desc: Let a gentle smile come to your face, even if it feels small.

items.label: Observation
items.desc: Notice five things you can see right now.

items.label: Colour
items.desc: Find something blue in the room.

items.label: Hand Tracing
items.desc: Slowly trace around your fingers with the other hand.

items.label: Listening
items.desc: Close your eyes and notice every sound around you.

items.label: Your Favourite
items.desc: Which one worked best for you? Remember it.

screens.heading: What We Learned: Mindfulness
screens.body: Mindfulness helps reduce stress, enhance focus and concentration, improve emotional regulation, reduce muscle tension, and encourage a positive outlook and improved self-esteem.

screens.heading: Building Self-Motivation
screens.body: Some days you feel pumped. Other days, not so much. Self-motivation is about finding little ways to keep going, even when you don't feel like it!

screens.heading: Did you know?
screens.body:
Even on days when you don't wake up feeling motivated. YOU CAN do things to encourage and buildd the skill of self motivation!

Feeling flat and unmotivated? Use ASMR!

items.title: Ask for help
items.body: Ask for help from others. Talk to a friend, teacher. Work next to someone focused. Goal buddy check-ins

items.title: Small steps
items.body: Take small steps or just the very next step. Set a timer. Break into mini steps. To do list

items.title: Mind talk
items.body: Take control of your inner voice. Positive self talk. Visualising success

items.title: Reward
items.body: Reward yourself at the end or celebrate your progress. Mini reward after task. Track progress with stickers of ticks. Do something fun when you finish

screens.heading: Which tool will work best for you?

items.label: You've been asked to run part of a school assembly, but you're feeling nervous and unsure where to start.
Your clss is working on a group project. But for some reason, you just don't feel like joining in.
you've set a big leadership goal, but it's still weeks away and you're loosing motivation.
You made a mistake last time you lead a group and now you're doubting yourself
Your coach asks you to give the pre-game address, and you're feeling pressure.

screens.heading: Leaning
screens.body: Self motivation isn't something you either have or don't, it's something you can build, using tools that work for you. You're not lazy or bad at something just because you feel like giving up. You might just need to try a different tool.

screens.heading: Social Awareness
screens.body: Social awareness is like having a special rader that helps you understand what's going on with other people around you. It means being able to pick up on their feelings, needs, and thoughts. It's like tuning into the unspoken cues in a conversation or sensing when someone might need a little extra support

skills.name: Observation

screens.heading: Perspective Switch
screens.intro:
Let's step into someone else's shoes and explore how different people might feel about certain situations.

 Let's keep it respectful and kinds, and do our best to try and understand a different perspective.

scenarios.title: The Group Chat Blow-Up: A message in your group chat gets misunderstood and someone feels left out. A joke turns into an argument.
views: The person who made the joke
An adult who hears about it later

scenarios.title: Group Work: Someone in your group isn't doing their fair share of the work and seems really quiet and withdrawn.
views: Other contributing members of the team
An adult overlooking the group dynamics

scenarios.title: No Phones at School: The school has a strict no-phones policy, and a student gets caught checking theirs between classes.
views: A friend who saw it happen
The school principal who set the rule

screens.body: Understanding another person's point of view doesn't mean we always have to agree, but it helps us communicate more respectfully, build stronger connections, and make fairer, more thoughtful decisions

screens.heading: Activity: Unhelpful and Helpful
screens.activity: Let's consider a scenario and explore what emotion could appear, an unhelpful reaction, and what a relpful response would look like

screens.title: You post online and someone writes a mean comment
screens.unhelpful: Write a nasty comment back or delete post
screens.helpful: Take a break before responding, talk to a trusted adult or friend, remind yourself that one comment doesn't define your worth

screens.title: Your friend tells you they don't want to hang out today
screens.unhelpful: Tell them you don't ever want to hang out again
screens.helpful: Find other people to hang out with, check if they're okay, read a book solo

screens.body: Emotional regulating means noticing your feelings and choosing how to respond, instead of just reacting. When you can manage your emotions, you think more clearly, stay clamer, and make better choices, even when things get tough.

screens.heading: Relationship Management
screens.body: Relationship management is like being a good team captain. It's about working well with others, whether it's with friends, family, or classmates. It means communicating effectively, solving problems together, and being their for each other. It's like keeping the team spirit alive by treating everyone with kindness and respect.

items.name: Communication
items.desc: Communicate openly and honestly tp build trust and understanding.

items.name: Active Listening
items.desc: Show genuine interest and empathy in conversations. Give all of your attention, concentrate, undertand, respond remember.

items.name: Conflict Resolution
items.desc: Resolve conflicts constructively by finding solutions that work for everyone involved.

items.name: Heathy Relationships
items.desc: Set boundaries and respect others' boundaries to maintain healthy reationships.

items.name: Appreciation
items.desc: Show appreciation and support for others, acknowledge their contributions and efforts.

items.name: Connect
items.desc: Build connections by being reliable, dependable, and compassionate in your interactions.

screens.heading: Relationship Management: What We Learned
screens.body:
Relationship management is about working well with others, even when we don't all agree. Communicating clearly, listening respectfully, and understand different points of view.

When we build healthy relationships, we feel more connected, we work better as a team, and we learn to appreciate the strengths and ideas that others bring.

screens.heading: Values Scenarios
screens.instruction: Reflect on each question, then share with the group
scenarios: A Genie in a bottle appears and grants you 3 wishes. What do you wish for?
If you could send a message to everyone on earth, what would it be?
Would you rather speak in front of the whole school OR have a difficult one-one-one conversation?
Would you rather be a leader who inspires people OR one who gets things done?
Would you rather be the captain of a team that loses OR a team member of a team that wins?
Would you rather loudly lead a team from the front OR support quietly behind the scenes?

screens.heading: What we learned
screens.body: Understanding ourselves helps us recognise what truly matters to us. By identifying and sharing our values, traits, and strengths we learn how our choices, actions, and relationships align with what we stand for.
